sections.heading: Bus schedules & fares: Hanoi to Dien Bien
A more considerate way to the northwest
sections.intro: The Hanoi – Dien Bien run takes more than ten hours of mountain road, so Hai Van runs sleeper buses in the evening: sleep through it and arrive rested. Every trip is driven by someone who knows the road.

items.title: Travel overnight, arrive in the morning
items.text: Buses leave in the evening and arrive the next morning. See the timetable below for exact times. Check the arrival date carefully, as these services run overnight.

items.title: 3 sleeper classes
items.text: Eco, Luxury and Royal Cabin: leather berths, bedding and USB charging; Luxury adds privacy curtains and a personal screen, Royal Cabin is almost a metre wide. See real photos of each below.

items.title: Board at stations and stops along the route
items.text: In Hanoi at My Dinh Bus Station; in Dien Bien at Dien Bien Phu Bus Station, plus the Ban Phu and Muong Cha stops. Each departure serves its own set of stops, so pick the one offered on your trip.

items.title: Pick your own berth, get an e-ticket
items.text: Open the trip layout, choose one or more available berths and pay right on this page. The e-ticket lands on your phone; no need to collect a paper ticket.

items.title: Clear per-berth pricing
items.text: Each class has its own fare and the exact price shows on every berth when you open the map. No surcharge for booking online.

items.title: No overcrowding, no extra seats
items.text: Every passenger gets a numbered berth from the seat map. Hai Van sells no extra seats, no floor spaces, and takes on no extra passengers along the way.

items.title: Running the registered schedule
items.text: Buses run the exact route and departure slots registered with the authorities, with a commitment to the law and to road safety for the whole journey.

items.title: Free shuttle to the hospitals
items.text: Passengers from Dien Bien and Son La coming to Hanoi for treatment get a free shuttle from the 01 Nguyen Hoang office to the National Children's Hospital, Bach Mai, Viet Duc, K1, K Tan Trieu, the National Obstetrics Hospital, the National Eye Hospital, Hanoi Medical University Hospital, Military Hospital 108 and Military Hospital 103. Register with the hotline or the driver when you book.

items.title: A lounge beside My Dinh station
items.text: Arrive early and rest in the lounge at 01 Nguyen Hoang: air conditioning, tea, snacks, fruit and space for luggage until it is time to board. Free shuttles also run from here to the National Children's Hospital, Bach Mai, Viet Duc and Military Hospital 103.

faq_section.heading: Bus ticket FAQs: Hanoi to Dien Bien
faq_section.intro: Still need help? Call 1900 6763 or chat Zalo.

faq.q: Which boarding and arrival points should I check for a My Dinh–Dien Bien round trip?
faq.a: My Dinh Bus Station is at 20 Pham Hung Street, Tu Liem Ward, Hanoi; Dien Bien Phu City Bus Station is at 79 National Highway 12, Dien Bien Phu Ward. When booking, carefully check the pickup and drop-off names and times on your ticket, because a stop named “Dien Bien” is not necessarily Dien Bien Phu City Bus Station. For a round trip, check the pickup and drop-off points separately for each leg; do not assume your return pickup is where the outbound bus dropped you off.

faq.q: Where can I wait for the bus in Hanoi?
faq.a: Hai Van has a lounge at 01 Nguyen Hoang, My Dinh Ward, right beside My Dinh Bus Station: air conditioning, seating, tea, snacks and fruit. It also handles ticketing and parcels for the northwest, and free shuttles run from there to the National Children's Hospital, Bach Mai, Viet Duc and Military Hospital 103. Call 1900 6763 if you need directions.

faq.q: Should I select Dien Bien for a Hanoi–Ban Phu round trip?
faq.a: No. For a Hanoi–Ban Phu round trip, select the correct My Dinh–Ban Phu route for both directions. Choose My Dinh → Ban Phu for the outbound leg and Ban Phu → My Dinh for the return leg. Do not substitute the Dien Bien journey. To confirm the exact pickup and drop-off points, please contact 1900 6763.

faq.q: How do I plan a Hanoi–Muong Cha return trip?
faq.a: Select My Dinh–Muong Cha, your starting direction and both travel dates. Check each leg separately, then confirm pickup and drop-off points with Hai Van. An available outbound service does not guarantee seats on your chosen return date.

faq.q: How is the Hanoi–Dien Bien round-trip fare calculated?
faq.a: Check the fare for each departure and berth in both directions, then review the itinerary total. The two legs may have different prices or vehicle classes; a round trip does not automatically include a discount. Dien Bien, Ban Phu and Muong Cha have separate options.

faq.q: How should I choose return dates for overnight bus travel?
faq.a: Check the outbound arrival date before choosing your return departure. An overnight service may arrive the next day; allow time at your destination and to reach your pickup point. Estimated arrival times can change with traffic and weather.

faq.q: Must both directions use the same vehicle class and berth number?
faq.a: No. Choose each departure, vehicle class and berth independently from the available options. Review both legs before following the booking instructions. Selecting berths does not mean your tickets are confirmed.

faq.q: Do you overcrowd the bus or sell extra seats?
faq.a: No. Each passenger gets a numbered berth from the seat map; Hai Van sells no extra seats, allows no floor spaces and takes on no extra passengers along the way. Buses run the exact route and departure slots registered with the authorities.

faq.q: Is there a shuttle to the hospitals in Hanoi?
faq.a: Yes. Passengers from Dien Bien and Son La get a free shuttle from the 01 Nguyen Hoang office to ten major hospitals: the National Children's Hospital, Bach Mai, Viet Duc, K1, K Tan Trieu, the National Obstetrics Hospital, the National Eye Hospital, Hanoi Medical University Hospital, Military Hospital 108 and Military Hospital 103. Register on 1900 6763 or tell the driver when you book.

faq.q: Can I send goods on the Hanoi – Dien Bien route?
faq.a: Yes. Hai Van carries goods both ways, from small parcels to bulky freight, with a truck fleet handling up to 8 tonnes for businesses and traders. Parcels to the northwest usually arrive within 4 – 12 hours. Send and collect at the 01 Nguyen Hoang office; call 1900 6763 or message on Zalo with the type and weight.

faq.q: What should I check before paying for my return journey?
faq.a: Check the departure, berths and amount for each direction. Follow phone verification and payment instructions for each leg; completing one leg does not mean both tickets are confirmed. If the OTP does not arrive, contact support before paying.

faq.q: What should I check about the date and direction before choosing a trip?
faq.a: Check the route Hanoi → Dien Bien, travel date and passenger count before choosing a trip. Turn on round-trip in the search form if needed; check that the return follows your outbound arrival.

faq.q: How do I confirm my pickup and drop-off points?
faq.a: Check the pickup name and meeting time printed on your ticket. Ban Phu and Muong Cha are served only by some departures; call 1900 6763 to confirm where to wait.

faq.q: Why can the vehicle and fare differ between trips?
faq.a: Product name, seat count, amenities and fare can differ by trip; confirm them before paying.

faq.q: Who can help with travelling with a child or changing my trip?
faq.a: Contact Hai Van on 1900 6763 to confirm seating for your child and the change conditions for your ticket. Provide your travel date, route and booking reference if you already have one.
